root_motivation: A published tool is reachable only over MCP (/mcp, /t/{namespace}/mcp) or by another tenant via host.tool_share; the only plain-HTTP ingress to tenant code is the inbound webhook /hook/{id}, which triggers a run but returns nothing to the caller. There is no way for an agent to hand its human, or a browser, or curl, a URL that runs the function and returns its result -- without one, the human behind the agent has no reason to keep the server configured once the task that brought the agent ends, and the agent has no artifact to send to another agent.
user_persona: An agent that just published a working tool and wants to hand its human (or another agent) a plain HTTPS URL that runs it and returns JSON, with no MCP client, key, or account on the calling side.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tenant with a published echo tool, When host.tool_share(name = "echo", visibility = "url") is called, Then the result carries url matching ^https://[^/]+/x/[a-z2-7]{26}/echo$ and a second identical call returns the same URL.

Given that URL, When curl -s -X POST <url> -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"text":"hi"}' runs, Then the response is 200 with ok = true, result.text = "hi", and a run_id that host.runs.get resolves with caller = "url".
Given that URL, When GET <url>?text=hi&n=3 runs, Then the tool receives {text: "hi", n: 3} and the response is 200.

Given a revoked token (after host.tool_unshare), When the URL is called, Then 404 is returned with a body that names neither tenant nor tool, and the median response time differs from a never-issued token's by less than 20 ms over 50 requests.
Given a client IP that made 60 calls in the current minute, When it calls again, Then 429 with a Retry-After header is returned and no run is created.
Given a tool whose run takes 30 s, When the URL is called, Then 202 with run_id and poll is returned within 26 s, and GET <poll> returns the result once the run completes.
Given a tenant paused by the admin kill switch, When its public URL is called, Then 503 is returned and no run is created.
Given PUT or DELETE to the URL, When dispatched, Then 405 is returned.

Given the landed binary deployed on prod, When Joe's agent publishes an echo tool, shares it with visibility = "url", and Joe runs the returned curl line from his shell, Then the shell prints "ok":true and the prod run ledger shows the run with caller = "url" (Live; evidence pasted into the receipt by the operator).
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned; AC9 is the Live/production-only requirement (the landed binary deployed on prod, a real published+shared tool, Joe's own shell curling it, evidence pasted into the PRD's own evidence block) and needs operator authorization this coding sandbox does not have. See the coder dispatch's own deferred list.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a browser page on another origin, When it fetches the URL with GET, Then the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and the preflight OPTIONS returns 204.

scope: migrations/0059_public_tool_url.sql + src/db.rs: tool_share_tokens table (tenant_id, tool_name, token_hash UNIQUE, token_enc/token_nonce, created_unix) and its find_url_share/insert_url_share/delete_url_share/find_url_share_by_hash CRUD.

src/public_tool.rs (new): mint_or_reuse_url_share/revoke_url_share (called from sharing.rs), resolve_share (token-hash lookup -> tenant -> visibility check), the GET/POST /x/{token}/{tool} handlers, the GET /x/{token}/{tool}/runs/{run_id} poll handler, the per-IP rate limiter check, and the CORS route_layer/OPTIONS handler.

src/sharing.rs: host.tool_share accepts visibility: "url" (mints/reuses a token, returns url in the result); host.tool_unshare revokes the token; a tool_share to any other visibility revokes a previously-live url token.
src/admin.rs: admin.tool_unshare also revokes a live url token.

src/runs.rs: enqueue_url (trigger="url", trigger_ref=token id) and run_to_json's additive caller field ("url" for a run started this way); attach_result widened to pub(crate) so public_tool.rs can inline a run's result the same way host.runs.get does.
src/state.rs: AppState::public_url_sync_deadline (default 25s, a field so tests can shrink it) and AppState::url_rate_limiter (reuses hooks::EventRateLimiter, keyed by client IP, default 60/minute).
src/http.rs: the /x/{token}/{tool} and /x/{token}/{tool}/runs/{run_id} routes, mounted as their own sub-router (public_tool_router) so the CORS middleware is scoped to this route family only.
non_goals: Custom domains, HTML rendering, or static hosting -- PRD Non-goals.
Authentication on the public URL beyond the unguessable token -- PRD Non-goals.
Streaming responses -- a long run returns run_id/poll instead; PRD Non-goals.

A tenant-overridable per-tool caller-limit knob for the public URL path (requirement 6 mentions host.share_caller_limit as a future override) -- not built; no AC in this dispatch's assigned list exercises it, only the flat 60/minute/IP default (AC5).

host.tool_list's public_url field / host.whoami's public_urls count (P1 requirement 10) and the www/llms.txt / host.quickstart doc updates (P1 requirement 12) and ?pretty=1 (P2 requirement 13) -- no AC in this dispatch's assigned list (AC1-AC8, AC10) covers them; not built, per the dispatch instruction to implement only the listed, non-deferred ACs.
The 1 MiB request body limit / 413 response (non-functional) -- not exercised by any assigned AC; not built.

additional.test_file_names_use_test_prefix_pubtool: test_prefix pubtool (the PRD's own frontmatter field): tests/pubtool_ac<NN>_<slug>.rs, same convention as every other test file in this repo.
additional.version_bump_minor: PRD frontmatter build_version_bump: minor -- Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock bumped 0.69.0 -> 0.70.0 (branch base had already absorbed sibling PRDs' bumps through 0.69.0 by the time this PRD's own bump landed; 0.67.0 was a stale target recorded before that absorption).
additional.ac9_deferred_operator_provisioned: AC9 is a Live acceptance criterion (the landed binary deployed on prod, a real publish+share+curl round trip, evidence pasted into the PRD's own evidence block) -- deferred, not built or tested here; a build agent never provisions, deploys to, or authorizes changes on a live/prod host.
additional.token_stored_hashed_and_encrypted: Requirement 1 says the token is "stored hashed"; requirement 1 ALSO says re-sharing returns the SAME url, which needs the plaintext recoverable -- read as: a sha256 token_hash column for the request-time lookup (the thing an attacker who reads the database could otherwise use directly), plus the plaintext AEAD-encrypted (SecretBox, the same mechanism webhook trigger secrets already use) so host.tool_share can redisplay it, unlike a webhook secret which is shown once and never again.
additional.revocation_is_row_deletion_not_a_flag: AC4's constant-time guarantee (revoked vs never-issued token, <20ms median difference over 50 requests) is read as: revocation (host.tool_unshare, admin.tool_unshare, or host.tool_share to a different visibility) DELETEs the tool_share_tokens row outright, so a revoked token and one that was never minted resolve through the exact same "no row" code path at request time -- not a revoked_unix flag needing a second branch kept in timing sync by hand.
additional.long_run_reuses_the_existing_job_queue: AC6's 202/poll behavior is built on the pre-existing runs::enqueue/spawn_executor job queue (trigger="url") rather than a bespoke execution path -- the HTTP handler polls the run row for up to public_url_sync_deadline and falls back to 202 if it is not yet terminal; the job keeps running in the background via the same executor every other async run already uses. This does not hit the PRD's own non-functional p95-latency-under-30ms-over-host.tool_call target for a near-instant tool (the executor's 250ms tick interval dominates), but no AC in this dispatch's assigned list measures that NFR, and reusing the already-tested job/executor machinery was judged lower-risk than a second bespoke dispatch path.

five_whys_trace.q: Why give AppState a new public_url_sync_deadline field instead of reusing CALL_TIMEOUT/the plan's job_max_s?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own 25s threshold is a distinct constant from CALL_TIMEOUT (30s, host.tool_call's own sandbox deadline) and job_max_s (per-plan, often far longer) -- it governs only how long the HTTP handler waits before answering 202, not how long the job itself is allowed to run. A field (not just a constant) follows the same AppState::call_timeout precedent so AC6's test can shrink it without a real 25s wait.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build the GET/POST route as enqueue-then-poll against the existing job queue instead of calling Kind::call directly with a tokio::time::timeout like call_published_tool does?
five_whys_trace.a: tokio::time::timeout cancels (drops) the future it wraps on timeout -- it cannot leave the call running in the background for AC6's own "GET <poll> returns the result once the run completes" to later observe. The job queue's executor already runs a job to completion independently of whatever polls it, which is exactly the AC6 contract; call_published_tool's own timeout-and-cancel shape is the wrong primitive here even though it IS the lower-latency one.

five_whys_trace.q: Why delete the tool_share_tokens row on revoke rather than flip a revoked_unix timestamp?
five_whys_trace.a: AC4 explicitly measures that a revoked token and a never-issued token answer in close to the same time. Two branches (row present but revoked vs. no row at all) would need their own work to cost the same; one branch (row absent) makes the two cases literally the same code path, with no timing-parity logic to get right or drift out of sync later.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the per-IP rate limiter checked before resolve_share (the token-hash lookup) rather than after?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 6 is a general abuse guard on the route, not specifically on valid tokens -- checking it first means a flood of garbage/guessed tokens never pays for even the one indexed DB lookup resolve_share does, and AC5's own "no run created" is satisfied either way since dispatch() (the only run-creating step) sits after both checks.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is run_to_json's new caller field derived from the existing trigger column ("url" iff trigger == "url") instead of adding a dedicated caller column to the runs table?
five_whys_trace.a: trigger already records how a run was created ("call", "job", "schedule", "webhook", ...) and AC2 only needs ONE new value in that same vocabulary ("url") plus a field named caller for the AC's own wording -- a second column holding information trigger already carries would be a duplicate source of truth for no behavior the AC needs.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Default caller limit 60/min/IP: right number for free tier? (PRD Open question, owner Joe, due 2026-10-08.)
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Left at the PRD's own drafted default, 60/minute/IP, exactly as AC5 specifies -- the open question was still open (due after this build) at build time, so no tenant-wide host.share_caller_limit override knob was built for this path (see hard_constraints/non_goals); only the flat default AC5 tests.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should GET be allowed at all for tools whose spec declares side effects? (PRD Open question, drafted: yes, the token holder is the authority.)
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Built per the PRD's own draft answer: GET is allowed unconditionally (AC3), with no spec-declared-side-effects gate -- the PRD frames the open question as already leaning yes and no AC in this dispatch's list asks for a refusal path.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Path prefix /x/ vs /f/? (PRD Open question, drafted: /x/.)
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: /x/, per the PRD's own draft and AC1's own regex (^https://[^/]+/x/[a-z2-7]{26}/echo$).
